newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House budget document sees deficit up in 1998.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House budget document sees deficit up in 1998.

text.p: The House Budget Committee expects the federal deficit to rise in fiscal 1998 to $90.2 billion and then steadily decline, reaching a $1.2 billion surplus in 2002, according to a document put together by committee Republicans.
The document was handed to House Republicans during a caucus to discuss a five-year plan to balance the budget.
Talks between White House and congressional budget negotiators were to continue in the afternoon to resolve remaining differences on the budget deal.
The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) predicts the deficit in fiscal 1997 will be $67 billion.
The House Budget Committee summary said the budget plan would mean an $89.2 billion deficit in fiscal 1999, an $82.4 billion deficit in 2000, and a $52.2 billion deficit in 2001.
The budget plan was based on CBO economic assumptions and assumes gross domestic product growth of 2.1 percent a year, the budget paper said.
The House budget document reaffirmed that the plan did not require any legislated change in the consumer price index (CPI).
"The plan anticipates CPI corrections as a result of statistical improvements assumed to be independently implemented by the Bureau of Labor Statistics," the budget paper said.
The CPI corrections were expected to be 0.3 percentage points starting in 2000, resulting in deficit reduction of about $15 billion for 2000 to 2002, the House budget paper said.
